epigraph: The wind breaks the weight of the stone.
vignette: The scribe stands on the shifting ridge. The stack rises in jagged layers of old wars. Below, heavy Umbral warforms press upward. They are dense with appetite and coal. The scribe carves the shape of a bird into the glass soil. The lines are sharp. The raptor takes form. It has no flesh. It is made of clear silica and wind. It spreads its wings. The air thins. The pressure from the ground below drops. The heavy enemies slow. They cannot crush the thin air. The Galeharrier circles the spire. It does not strike. It holds the space open. The Verdant truth insists on lightness. The heavy ground tries to bury the bird. The glass feathers vibrate. The pressure breaks. The raptor glides over the debris. It is not a soldier. It is a law of air. The ground believes in lift. The weight is halved. The enemies stagger in the thinning. The truth holds.
codex_note: The Galeharrier proves that conviction can alter gravity, reducing the crushing weight of opposing inscriptions by half through the imposition of aerial law.
